title: Film Festival Programming Desk
description: Submissions, screenings, venues, guests and volunteers for a film festival.

spec.useCase: Lucinda Brightwater-Osei directs a regional film festival and uses this to see which submissions still need a decision, which screenings are scheduled and which guests have not confirmed travel.

text.text: The festival from call for entries to closing night. Start with the Dashboard each morning. Decide submissions before their date, schedule only selected films, and confirm every guest's travel two weeks ahead.

text.text: A festival is a countdown. Work backward from opening night and tick off each phase.

Publish the schedule and open ticket sales

text.text: Open the Dashboard. If a decision date has passed, decide it. If a guest has not confirmed, call.
Fair review means every film gets the same attention. Use the same score sheet for everyone.
Assign each film to two reviewers. Press Start review.
Each reviewer gives a score from 1 to 10 and writes two lines.
The programmer averages the scores and enters one number.
Press Select, Waitlist or Decline and send the notice.
On festival days the work is people and time. A written checklist keeps each venue calm.
Two hours before the first show
Test projection, sound and subtitles with the real file
Set up the box office and accessible seating
Reset the room and check the next film's file.
Count tickets and write the total on the screening.
Walk the room and the lobby for safety.
Press Mark held on each screening
Lock the booth and return keys
